chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Amir Al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'Regarding the male part of the child is the (complete) wergild, and regarding the male part of an impotent man is the (complete) wergild'.
ai.seo_question: What is the blood money ruling for injury to the male reproductive organ in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) reports that Imam Ali (AS) ruled that injury to the male organ of a young boy or an impotent man incurs the complete wergild (diyah al-kamilah). This ruling is significant in Shia jurisprudence as it establishes that the functional capacity for procreation, rather than age or current potency, determines the full value of the organ for blood money purposes.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Regarding a male part of the child is the (complete) wergild, and regarding the male part of an impotent man is the (complete) wergild’.
